newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Anti-Bhutto coalition takes her home province.
newsitem.headline: Anti-Bhutto coalition takes her home province.

text.p: A coalition led by new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's party took power in Pakistan's volatile southern province of Sindh on Saturday, denying ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto a foothold in her home base.

The province's new Chief Minister Liaquat Jatoi, a member of Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party, took the oath of office at the head of a coalition with the militant ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and some smaller groups.
Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP), despite its rout in the general elections on February 3, remains the single largest group with 35 deputies in the 109-seat Sindh provincial assembly.
But its prospects of putting together a coalition were dashed when the 14-seat PML reached a power-sharing agreement on Wednesday with the 28-seat MQM and some other groups and independent deputies.
The PML had already formed a government in the populous central province of Punjab and leads a coalition in North West Frontier province with the left-wing Awami National Party.
The only province with a non-PML government is Baluchistan in the southwest, where nationalist groups formed a coalition on Saturday with Akhtar Mengal as chief minister.
